:::{#def-outer-product}
#### Outer product

The **outer product** of a vector $\vecf{u}$ of length $m$
and a vector $\vecf{v}$ of length $n$
is the $m \times n$ matrix product (@def-matrix-mult) $\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}$
of the column vector $\vecf{u}$ with the row vector $\tp{\vecf{v}}$.
Its entries are

$$
\paren{\underbrace{\vecf{u}}_{m \times 1}\,\underbrace{\tp{\vecf{v}}}_{1 \times n}}_{ij}
= u_i v_j
\qquad \text{(definition of matrix multiplication; the sum has one term)}
$$

:::

::: notes
The dot product $\tp{\vecf{u}}\vecf{v}$ (@exm-dot-product-matmul)
needs two vectors of the same length and gives a number.
The outer product $\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}$
takes vectors of any two lengths and gives a matrix
[@banerjee2014linear, Chapter 1, p. 11].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-outer-product}
#### An outer product

For $\vecf{u} = (1, 2, 3)$ and $\vecf{v} = (4, 5)$:

$$
\ba
\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of the outer product)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix}
1 \cd 4 & 1 \cd 5 \\
2 \cd 4 & 2 \cd 5 \\
3 \cd 4 & 3 \cd 5
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(entry } (i, j) \text{ is } u_i v_j \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix}
4 & 5 \\
8 & 10 \\
12 & 15
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

:::
